entry.description: OpenAI Math family 370, The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures. OpenAI's 6 October 2026 catalogue reports: Resolves the subcritical Lane–Emden conjecture and its weighted Hénon extension. entry.description: An $n^{0.3+\varepsilon}$-Approximation for Steiner $k$-Forest. entry.description: Network Coding Can Beat Routing in Undirected Multiple-Unicast Networks. The paper reports a counterexample to the 2004 Li–Li conjecture: a finite connected simple undirected network with unit shared edge capacities, maximum degree three and distinct leaf terminals admits a binary linear block code with common rate strictly above fractional routing. The stated tooth-restricted variant is also hard. Further checking: Independently verify the 3-SAT reduction, gadget consistency, subtour feasibility and NP-membership witness encoding. Establish exact novelty/priority for unrestricted versus restricted comb separation. Do not infer hardness for larger inequality families merely from comb separation. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. entry.description: A uniform zero-free half-plane for Dedekind and finite-order Hecke L-functions. The current owner source reports: For every number field K, the current owner source reports that its Dedekind zeta function has no zeros in Re(s)>31/32, excluding the pole s=1. It also reports the same half-plane for finite-order Hecke L-functions represented by ray class characters with nonzero modulus; s=1 is included for nonprincipal characters, whose continuations are entire. The compared statements identify the continuations with the Dedekind zeta function or ideal Dirichlet series in Re(s)>1. This is not the full generalized Riemann hypothesis. Direct AI contribution: Dean Cureton and Jesse Thorner directed the mathematical research and judgments; the reread owner README and metadata expressly attribute proof generation and Lean formalization to AxiomProver under human direction. Further checking: The pinned owner revision 09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d dated 13 October strengthens the earlier registered 5999/6000 checkpoint to 31/32 and adds heckeCorollary to comparator.json. The stale registry checkpoint is not the latest compared scope. Independently audit analytic continuation, the ray-class-character/finite-order-Hecke identification, principal-character pole exceptions and the metaplectic/automorphic and reused-source dependencies. The versioned Hexagon manuscript previously returned HTTP403; its exact revised informal correspondence and Section15 allocation have not been independently read here. Owner-reported builds, standard-axiom assertions and agent reviews are not independent verification or human peer review. Preserve the October12 first-public date and provisional=1, low strict confidence, reviewStatus unreviewed, no strict Superhuman override. No downloaded proof artifact was executed.

entry.description: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital nets in every dimension. The source reports: For every s >= 3 and integer base q whose prime factors are at least s-1, explicit digital (0,sk,s)-nets with q^(sk) points have covering radius at most sqrt(s)N^(-1/s). For q >= 5a_s+4 they have toroidal and Euclidean separation at least (1-a_s/q)N^(-1/s), with the source’s explicit dimension-dependent a_s and restricted first-order sharpness. This does not assert the separation bound for every small admissible base or every arbitrary cardinality. Direct AI connection: Leonhard Gruenschloss’s README explicitly states Claude Opus 5.5 produced the constructions, proofs and formalization under author direction, with early Claude Fable 5.1 exploration. Further checking: Check admissible-base restrictions, the Babai-rounded column construction, separation/covering and first-order sharpness. Read the complete historical open-problem source and establish priority; author signoff is for the headline statement, not independent peer review of every proof. entry.description: Rigidity, signed-weight and stability extensions for qubit cloning. The source reports: Beyond the classical 5/6 universal cloning and asymmetric trade-off bounds, the source reports uniqueness under the six-Pauli-state average-fidelity criterion, signed real-weight asymmetric inequalities with (2a+b)(a+2b)>=0 and equality classification, and stability: average fidelity at least 5/6-epsilon implies total squared Kraus distance to the Buzek–Hillery span at most 6epsilon and channel Frobenius distance at most 200sqrt(epsilon)||rho||_F. The result uses finite Kraus families; it does not newly discover the classical cloning bound, establish Choi–Kraus, or identify six-state averages with Bloch-sphere averages. The source reports: Huang and Peng report uniform short-time pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metric has Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius, without an a priori evolving curvature bound. Check exact correspondence to Chen’s historical question; this does not assert uniqueness from arbitrary complete initial metrics without the stated conditions. entry.description: Generators of separable unital C*-algebras. The source reports: Elliott, Li and Niu report that, assuming the recent separable-predual II1-factor single-generation theorem, a separable unital C*-algebra with nonempty compact zero-dimensional extreme trace boundary has two ordinary generators under strict comparison of positive elements. With real rank zero and strict comparison of projections it is singly generated with norm-dense G-delta single generators. A separate atomless full-spectrum unitary and vanishing small-corner conditional-expectation compression hypothesis yields single generation, including reduced free-group C*-algebras for 2 through countably infinitely many generators. Direct AI connection: The paper directly states that the work was carried out using ChatGPT; mathematical stages and exact model are not specified. Further checking: Audit the assumed II1-factor generation theorem and the precise small-corner compression hypothesis; a Haar unitary alone is explicitly insufficient. Establish theorem-level AI materiality, original priority and the claimed free-product applications. Do not generalize this to every separable C*-algebra or confuse two ordinary with two self-adjoint generators. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: An elementary proof of geometric bulk conductances in even dimensions. The source reports: Drouot reports an independent elementary proof of the recent Martinian–Stoiber geometric Kubo conductance identity in every even dimension: for the stated short-range projectors and transverse open-set families, geometric conductance is the topological intersection integer times bulk conductance. The proof deforms cochains using Stokes, Poincare and Kitaev’s algebraic identity, rather than newly discovering the already-reported conductance formula. Direct AI connection: The author explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5 with almost the entire proof and describes his removal of an unnecessary part and subsequent organization. Further checking: Audit decay, trace-class and transversality hypotheses and the elementary cochain argument. Compare against Martinian–Stoiber to establish genuine independent proof novelty and chronology, not priority for the identity itself; the earlier theorem was learned of late. entry.description: Exact regret-profile frontier and finite-window prediction refinements. The source reports: Ozelim and coauthors report sharpenings and elementary additions to classical prediction theory. For a countable pairwise mutually singular source family, infinite-horizon expected log-loss regret profiles obey the Kraft inequality, every Kraft profile is attained by its subprobability Bayes mixture, and equality holds exactly for full-mass mixtures on every cylinder. entry.description: Counterexamples in heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause opinion dynamics. The source reports: Hegarty, Ognissanti and Wedin report explicit heterogeneous SBC and SBI opinion systems refuting Mirtabatabaei–Bullo’s eventual proximity-digraph freezing and eventual freezing-or-pseudostability conjectures, and the corresponding part of their published Theorem 6.4. The examples include convergent trajectories with indefinitely changing digraphs and constant-digraph trajectories that are not pseudostable. The main conjecture that every opinion vector converges remains open. Direct AI connection: Section 7 explicitly says Claude Opus 5.5 found all four examples under author prompting; the human authors wrote the paper and checked the examples by hand. Further checking: Independently verify the exact closed-neighborhood update inequalities and trajectories and compare the cited 2012 assertions. Do not promote auxiliary-conjecture disproofs to a disproof of convergence, or treat unverified background computations mentioned in Section 7 as established classifications. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Smaller and near-homogeneous Hegselmann–Krause counterexamples. The source reports: JD Jones reports new extensions beyond Hegarty–Ognissanti–Wedin: five-agent constant-digraph SBC and SBI counterexamples, a five-agent SBI complex-mode example oscillating about its limit in every five consecutive times, and a five-agent SBC family with unequal radii arbitrarily close to homogeneous that converges without freezing or pseudostability.
